nodes.label: Weakly-up member state
nodes.rationale: Breaks the deadlock where a joiner on a partitioned side waits forever for a leader it cannot see; it becomes visible via gossip inside its partition without the leader's involvement. Temporary — it converges to up once the leader is reachable, and can go straight to leaving/removed if stopped first.

nodes.label: weaklyUpAfterMs
nodes.rationale: Default 0 (disabled); 3-10s is typical. Must stay above the failure detector's unreachableAfterMs, otherwise routine gossip round-trip delays promote members and the leader's late answer demotes them again. Also settable as actor-ts.cluster.weakly-up-after, with the usual explicit options > HOCON > defaults order.

nodes.label: Passive participation, no active responsibilities
nodes.rationale: A weakly-up member can receive tells and subscribe to cluster events but cannot be a router routee, host sharding entities or win a singleton election. Deliberately conservative: it may actually be on the minority side of a partition, so letting it host a singleton would risk double leadership.

nodes.label: MemberWeaklyUp event
nodes.rationale: A non-zero rate in normal operation means partitions are happening — or the threshold is set too low for the network.

nodes.label: upMembers() excludes weakly-up
nodes.rationale: Code branching on 'are at least 3 members up?' can pass on one side of a partition and fail on the other; decide explicitly which states your logic treats as live.

nodes.label: Weakly-up is not a downing substitute
nodes.rationale: It helps a join make progress during a partition; it does nothing to resolve the partition, so a downing strategy is still needed to remove the losing side once it heals.
